claims.text: Non-alphanumerics collapse to single spaces before counting, so ``PKG_TURBO=1`` scores 1, not 12: punctuation and the value are not an explanation of what the switch turns on.
claims.why: The code in _described replaces name with space, then uses _ALNUM_RUN.sub(' ', rest).strip() to collapse non-alphanumerics to single spaces. For 'PKG_TURBO=1' after removing name, rest becomes '=1', then _ALNUM_RUN.sub(' ', '=1') yields ' 1', stripped to '1', length 1, matching the claim.

claims.text: Recorded in the snapshot so that a run narrowed by ``DAEDALUS_IGNORE`` can never be mistaken for a clean one.
claims.why: The claim about snapshot recording is not verifiable in this chunk; it refers to external snapshot storage.

claims.text: The env value is stored VERBATIM rather than hashed: the point is that a reviewer reading the failure can see what was hidden without re-running anything.
claims.why: The code returns the env value directly from os.environ.get(IGNORE_ENV, '').strip() without hashing, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: ``sites`` is runtime-only detail (file:line) used to make remedies actionable, and is deliberately kept OUT of the snapshot so line-number churn never produces a diff a human has to read.
claims.why: The claim about snapshot storage is not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: ``reach`` and ``switches`` are the reports this state was derived FROM, carried out so no caller has to re-run either engine to ask a follow-up question -- which is how two engines got built here in the first place.
claims.why: The claim about derivation from reach and switches is not verifiable in this chunk.

observations.what: The _described method uses _ALNUM_RUN.sub(' ', rest).strip() to measure length of prose. The docstring example claims 'PKG_TURBO=1' scores 1, which matches the code behavior.
ignore_config returns a dict with 'env' and 'file' keys, where 'file' is a hex digest of file content or empty string. The docstring claims it is a comparable fingerprint.
ScanResult docstring claims sites is kept out of snapshot, but this is unverifiable from this chunk.
